items.body: Wore lavender mullet, brought smiles to patients shooting puck from left circle ARLINGTON, Va. -- Alex Ovechkin 's office was open for visitors during the Washington Capitals' annual Hockey Fights Cancer skate at MedStar Capitals Iceplex on Thursday. Having the opportunity to shoot the puck with the NHL's all-time goal-scoring leader from his favorite spot in the left circle brought plenty of smiles from children impacted by cancer who participated in the skate with Capitals players. "To see how they smile, to see how they have fun, score goals, skate around, chat with us, it's very important and it's very cool," Ovechkin said. For the skate, each player was paired with a child from Blood Cancer United Mid-Atlantic, Make-A-Wish Mid-Atlantic, MedStar Health or Sunrise Day Camp Greater Washington. This year's skate was different, though, after Ovechkin, who holds the NHL record with 930 goals, announced Oct. 5 that this will be his final season in the League. So, instead of being paired with one child, the 41-year-old forward set up shop in the "Ovi's Office" station in the left circle, and each child took turns shooting from there. "The kids have fun," Ovechkin said. "They shoot the pucks. They (skate) around, smiling, laughing and their parents are happy, so it's very important." Ovechkin appeared to enjoy it as much as the children. Like some of them, their parents and his teammates, Ovechkin donned a lavender mullet wig to join the fun. "He's always got the biggest smile out there and has a great time," Capitals coach Spencer Carbery said. "I bet if you ask him in a few years … he'll miss days like this, being able to give back like this." items.title: Rangers put goalie James Reimer on waivers after one start
items.body: James Reimer ’s time with the New York Rangers appears to be coming to an end after making just one start that lasted one period. The Rangers put Reimer on waivers Thursday and could send him to Hartford of the American Hockey League if he is not claimed by one of the NHL’s other 31 clubs. Reimer was pulled after allowing three goals on eight shots in 20 minutes on the way to a home loss to Los Angeles on Oct. 26. New York late last month signed him to a contract for this season in the hopes that the 38-year-old could spell Dylan Garand, who had been playing almost nonstop since franchise goaltender Igor Shesterkin was lost for the season with a knee injury. Instead, Reimer struggled in his only chance, and Garand has played in 11 consecutive games. After posting a 1.85 goals-against average and .929 save percentage in his first six games, Garand is at 3.50 and .877 in his past five. Reimer going on waivers now seems to indicate Joonas Korpisalo is nearing a return from his lower-body injury. Korpisalo stopped 34 of the 37 shots he faced in a minor league rehab start with Hartford on Wednesday night. It was Korpisalo's injury during the first week of the season that set this goalie carousel in motion. The Rangers acquired him from Boston over the summer to back up Shesterkin, and Garand cleared waivers prior to opening night to go to the AHL's Wolf Pack and play regularly. Garand was recalled when Korpisalo got hurt and became the go-to option when Shesterkin went down.

items.title: Rangers waive James Reimer, place Sean Durzi on injured reserve
items.summary: Reimer will dress on Thursday night, as Joonas Korpisalo is set to return to the lineup.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Some roster moves on Broadway as an Original Six team prepares for an upcoming road trip. On Thursday, the New York Rangers placed goaltender James Reimer on waivers, making him available to the other 31 teams in the NHL. The team also put defenseman Sean Durzi on injured reserve. If Reimer clears waivers on Friday, he’ll be eligible to return to the Rangers’ American Hockey League affiliate, the Hartford Wolf Pack. He’s expected to back up Dylan Garand in Thursday night’s game against the Philadelphia Flyers , but with Joonas Korpisalo nearing a return to the lineup, the Rangers need to make room on their roster. Reimer signed a one-year contract with the Rangers last month, giving the team some depth at goaltending amid injury woes to Korpisalo and Igor Shesterkin . He’s dressed in four games, only making one start. That came last Monday, when he gave up three goals on eight shots against the Los Angeles Kings before being pulled after the first period. The 38-year-old’s cap hit is a prorated $850,000. He has already played one game for the Wolf Pack, a 35-save shutout against the Providence Bruins on Oct. 23. Durzi’s placement on IR is retroactive to Oct. 26, when he was in the lineup in a 6-3 loss to the Los Angeles Kings. He’s been plagued with an undisclosed injury that has forced him to miss the past two games, with the Rangers expecting the 28-year-old to miss even more time, as he’s not going to be joining the team on its upcoming four-game road trip through the Pacific Division, which begin on Saturday with a matchup against the Seattle Kraken . In 14 games this season, the Mississauga, Ont. native has scored two goals and five points, with a plus/minus of -1 while averaging 19:52 of ice time per game.

It wasn't as if Reinhart's rookie season in Buffalo was a failure; he posted 23 goals and 42 points in 79 games, and his point total eventually grew as high as 65 points in 82 games in 2018-19. However, as the Sabres' futility to even qualify for the Stanley Cup playoffs dragged on and on, Reinhart eventually wasn't seen as part of the solution for Buffalo. So when the Sabres traded Reinhart to the Florida Panthers for goalie Devon Levi and a 2022 first-round draft pick that turned into Jiri Kulich, some Sabres fans weren't all that upset to see him go. items.title: Flames activate goalie Devin Cooley, assign Arsenii Sergeev to AHL
items.body: The Calgary Flames activated goaltender Devin Cooley from injured reserve on Thursday, Sportsnet's Eric Francis reported. Arsenii Sergeev was assigned to the AHL's Calgary Wranglers in a corresponding move. Cooley has been out since he suffered a lower-body injury on Oct. 28 in a game against the Edmonton Oilers. Oilers forward Colton Dach crashed into Cooley with 12 seconds remaining in the opening 20 minutes and received a two-minute penalty for goaltender interference. Cooley remained in for the final 12 seconds but was not on the bench to start the second. He was then ruled out for the remainder of the game with a lower-body injury. The 29-year-old had been red-hot before he went down injured, allowing just six goals on 133 shots over his previous four starts. With Cooley out, Dustin Wolf started three of four games, picking up two wins. Cooley's first chance to return to the net will be on Friday when the Flames host the Anaheim Ducks.

items.body: The Minnesota Wild defenceman has reportedly been cleared to play by doctors, and is expected to join the team's upcoming three-game road trip, per The Athletic's Joe Smith . Faber, 23, has yet to play after suffering a skull fracture in the pre-season. He took a puck to the side of the head and has since missed a month of action. As for when exactly he could return, a date remains a "moving target" according to Smith, depending on how Faber's strength and conditioning ramps up after being off for over five weeks. When he does return, the former second-round pick is looking to build off a productive 2025-26 season. Faber played 80 games last year, logging career-highs in goals (15) and points (51). He then chipped in four more goals and six assists through 11 playoff appearances. Faber led all Wild blue-liners in goals scored last season and was second in total points, just two behind Quinn Hughes. He's looking to re-join a Minnesota team entering Thursday with an 11-3-3 record, good for 1st in the Central Division. Smith also reported that both Nick and Marcus Foligno, along with Filip Gustavsson and Jared Spurgeon are all expected to make their returns off injured reserve during the Wild's upcoming road trip.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images After making the playoffs last season for the first time since 2020 (going back to their time as the Arizona Coyotes), the Utah Mammoth were hoping to make the leap into legitimate Stanley Cup contention this year. Just over a month into this season, it appears they could be doing just that. Utah sits second in the competitive Central Division with 20 points through 16 games. Their top players, including forwards Clayton Keller, Nick Schmaltz, Logan Cooley, and defenseman Mikhail Sergachev, are all producing at over a point-per-game clip. While not a perfect team (they rank 23rd in the NHL with 3.37 goals allowed per game), the Mammoth have a chance to join the upper crust of the Western Conference if they continue to improve throughout the year. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sarah Boeke/PWHL Ahead of its fourth season of operation, the Professional Women’s Hockey League is making some changes to its rulebook. On Thursday, the league announced a few tweaks ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, including clarifications on body checking, mandated neck protection, new high-sticking rules, and some experimentation with overtime during the preseason. Neck guards have been a point of contention around the game ever since Adam Johnson’s tragic passing in 2023 . Since then, the IIHF , USA Hockey , American Hockey League and the NHL have mandated the use of neck guards for their athletes. Now, the PWHL is requiring all players and goaltenders to wear cut-resistant neck protection during games, including pregame warmups. An interesting rule being implemented this year is that players can now knock the puck out of the air with their stick above the shoulders. Unlike previous years, the play is blown dead after the puck is knocked down by a player and either that player or their teammate touches the puck. Now, play can continue, regardless of who bats the puck out of the air. Also, players can score when deflecting the puck high in the air, eliminating the judgment call from on- and off-ice officials about whether a player’s stick was above the crossbar. A similar rule was adopted by the WCHA prior to the 2025-26 season. One point in the rule is that players can cradle the puck above their shoulders (a la the Michigan goal). items.body: OneCourt’s technology allows fans to feel each play as it happens The NHL and Ticketmaster are teaming to bring complimentary OneCourt haptic tablets to blind and low-vision fans at all the League’s tentpole events in North America this season. OneCourt’s broadcast technology converts real-time game data into vibrations that allows fans to feel each play as it happens. Implementation of the program began with the 2026 Tim Horton’s NHL Heritage Classic between the Winnipeg Jets and Montreal Canadiens at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg, Manitoba on Oct. 25. It will continue at the Discover NHL Winter Classic between the Utah Mammoth and Colorado Avalanche at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City, Utah on Dec. 31, the 2027 Honda NHL All-Star Weekend at UBS Arena, home of the New York Islanders, on Feb. 5-6, and the 2027 Navy Federal Credit Union NHL Stadium Series between the Dallas Stars and Vegas Golden Knights at AT&T Stadium, home of the Dallas Cowboys, on Feb. 20. In addition, the Avalanche, Washington Capitals, Chicago Blackhawks and Detroit Red Wings will be the first NHL teams to offer OneCourt tablets to fans at their home games. "This partnership with the National Hockey League is a milestone achievement for accessibility in live sports," Kurt Schwartzkopf, head of sports at Ticketmaster, said. "Ticketmaster is proud to support our NHL partners in bringing this experience to life and advance our mission to make live events inclusive and accessible to every fan.” The NHL has been a leader in sports accessibility as the only major professional sports league to produce live game broadcasts in American Sign Language (ASL) through “NHL in ASL.” Now the League is joining Ticketmaster’s ongoing efforts to enhance the game-day experience for blind and low-vision fans.

items.title: Prospects Report: Why top 2028 NHL Draft prospect Liam Pue is ‘an electric player’
items.summary: At age 16, Regina Pats star Liam Pue already is one of the most dangerous players in the WHL. There’s every reason to believe he’ll be a high pick in the 2028 NHL Draft, writes Mike Koreen.
items.body: Liam Pue first put on skates and hit the ice at age two at home in Langley, B.C., in the arms of his father, Jason. Liam was a quick learner, so much so that his mom, Kristin, joked to her husband, "Geez, he almost skates better than he walks." Because of that early ability, and with Liam wanting to follow his brother Landon —three years older — into hockey, his parents looked for programs to help their youngest son improve his skills. There was one problem, though. "We went through a season where he's skating pretty well for his age, but there's no programs," Jason recalled this week. "I started signing him up for programs, but I lied about his age." "I remember one day my wife had taken him to a skate and there was kind of a new coach on the ice working with Liam," Jason said. "After the skate, this coach came up to the parent-viewing area, and he opened the door, and he said, 'Whose kid is wearing the Datsyuk jersey?' My wife just buried her head cause she was like, 'Oh my goodness, he knows we lied about his age.' Finally, she kind of waved, and he just came up, and he said, 'Your kid is awesome.'" That first meeting with coach Curtis Fraser, a former pro player and cousin of ex-NHLer Colin Fraser, turned out to be the start of a long, productive partnership. For years, Liam Pue played under Fraser up an age group or two with a familiar group of teammates. Pue continued working with Fraser at the Langley Hockey Academy as a teenager. That development path, with much of it outside the Hockey Canada umbrella, turned out to be a perfect fit for Pue. The 16-year-old winger is in the midst of a fantastic first full season in the WHL with the Regina Pats and is considered a top candidate for the 2028 NHL Draft, alongside fellow fast riser and Pats teammate Maddox Schultz.

This week, the puck will drop on the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship. After an exhilarating tournament at the Winter Olympics last February, everyone will be watching to see how the world’s best players perform in a restructured tournament. Gone are the tiered groups, where everyone in Group A advances to the quarterfinals. Now, with the snake format similar to the men’s tournaments, the United States and Canada will be on opposite sides of the preliminary stage, though almost everyone expects them to meet in the gold medal game on Nov. 16. items.body: BUFFALO, N.Y. — Michael Amadio scored on a wrist shot with 3:09 left to lead the Ottawa Senators to a 2-1 come-from-behind victory over the Buffalo Sabres on Wednesday night. Fabian Zetterlund and Tim Stutzle assisted on the go-ahead goal as Ottawa and Amadio capitalized on a 3-on-2 break. Shane Pinto also scored for the Senators, tying the game at 1 at 11:33 of the second period. Peyton Krebs scored at the 14-minute mark of the first to give the Sabres the lead. Tage Thompson and Zach Benson assisted on Krebs' first goal of the season. Samuel Ersson made 24 saves in the win for the Senators, who entered the game having lost three of their last four games, including a 6-3 setback against Anaheim on Sunday. Colten Ellis had 28 saves for the Sabres, who had their three-game win streak halted. Senators: Host the Utah Mammoth on Saturday in the opener of a three-game homestand. Sabres: Host the Columbus Blue Jackets on Friday in the second game of a four-game homestand.

items.title: Canadiens’ Ivan Demidov fractured ankle in preseason
items.summary: Demidov has been out since early October with a lower-body injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Fans of the Montreal Canadiens have finally received some clarity regarding an injury to one of their top players. On Wednesday’s episode of DFO Insider with Jeff Marek and David Pagnotta, Dan Milstein, the agent of Canadiens winger Ivan Demidov, revealed that Demidov suffered a fractured ankle during the preseason. Demidov, 20, has been out since early October with what was classified as a lower-body injury. Despite sustaining the injury in the preseason, the Russian national was active to start the regular season, putting up a goal and an assist in two games before initially getting ruled out for two to four weeks. Now in early November, we’re at the tail end of that time frame, but Milstein suggested that Demidov is still weeks away from returning. “Ivan Demidov is getting ready. Probably a few more weeks or so, we’ll see him back in the lineup,” Milstein said. “Unfortunately, he had a fractured ankle in the preseason. It was bothering him but he continued playing for the two games. I saw him after the first game of the season in Toronto, he walked up to me and said ‘Hey, something is bothering (me), something is not right.’ Then he goes out, plays the second game and we did an MRI. Hopefully Ivan will be back on the ice in a very short while and he’ll help the Montreal Canadiens start winning some games.” Demidov is coming off a sterling rookie season, in which he notched 19 goals and 43 assists for 62 points in all 82 regular season games, finishing second in voting for the Calder Trophy. He then contributed three goals and six assists for nine points in Montreal’s 19 playoff games. The Canadiens will host the Utah Mammoth on Thursday to finish up a three-game home stand .

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nikita Kucherov’s well-publicized trade request shook the hockey world last week. And now, his agent is shedding some light on the whole situation. Gold Star’s Dan Milstein joined Jeff Marek and David Pagnotta on Wednesday’s episode of DFO Insider, where he said the time is now for Kucherov to move on from the Tampa Bay Lightning – the only team the Russian winger has ever played for. “I can’t say anything bad about [Lightning GM Julien Brisebois ],” Milstein said. “I believe we’re on very, very good terms. We’ve done business for a very long time. And I’ll just leave it at that, guys.” Milstein didn’t elaborate on what happened for Kucherov to request a trade out of Tampa. The Lightning originally selected Kucherov in the second round of the 2011 NHL Draft. items.body: Register Login Red Wings Recall Michal Postava; Place Albert Johansson On IR By Brennan McClain | at November 4, 2026 5:30 pm The Detroit Red Wings announced they recalled netminder Michal Postava from the Grand Rapids Griffins in the AHL under emergency conditions. In a corresponding roster move, the Red Wings placed defenseman Albert Johansson on the injured reserve. It’s not a surprising transaction considering goaltender John Gibson left last night’s contest with a lower-body injury . In our coverage of Gibson’s injury, PHR’s Ryan Long wrote, “ Gibson allowed two goals on 11 shots while playing the entire first period, and it isn’t exactly clear when he was hurt. If he misses more time, Daniil Tarasov would take over as Detroit’s starter and the Red Wings would need to recall a goaltender from AHL Grand Rapids to fill out the roster. ” That’s exactly what Detroit did. Postava, 24, returns to the Red Wings after earning his first career win, a 4-3 shootout victory over the Edmonton Oilers on October 26th. In that contest, also his first professional start, Postava stopped 24 of 27 shots (.889 SV%). In the AHL, Postava has been flat-out dominant, taking home AHL Goalie of the Month honors after winning all five of his appearances with a .955 SV% and 1.20 GAA. Meanwhile, Johansson lands on the injured reserve, as expected. Fortunately, since his placement on the injured reserve is retroactive to October 24th, the Red Wings can activate him whenever he is healthy. He has already missed Detroit’s last five contests with an undisclosed injury.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Some prominent names are coming together to form an advisory group for Hockey Canada. According to a press release issued by Hockey Canada, the group will “provide mentorship, leadership and hockey acumen to the organization’s men’s, women’s and para hockey teams, and hockey operations department.” Cassidy had already been hired by Hockey Canada in September as a special advisor to Daniele Sauvageau, the general manager of the national women’s team. The Ottawa native was a head coach in the NHL for parts of nine seasons with the Boston Bruins and Vegas Golden Knights , winning a Stanley Cup with Vegas in 2023. He also served as an assistant coach for the Canadian men’s national team at the 4 Nations Face-Off in 2025 and the Winter Olympics in 2026. Yzerman is currently a senior advisor for the Detroit Red Wings after stepping down as the team’s general manager in July. The Cranbrook, B.C. native served as Detroit’s general manager for seven seasons, and previously served as the Tampa Bay Lightning ‘s general manager for eight seasons. items.title: Jets hoping for confidence boost from historic win: ‘We’re not looking back’
items.summary: The Jets entered Tuesday’s game against the Canadiens at an all-time low. But then the they pulled out a miracle, which could be just the kind of confidence boost the team needed.
items.body: WINNIPEG — The Winnipeg Jets have stopped the bleeding — for now. The Jets pulled off the impossible on Tuesday, scoring four goals over a span of just two minutes and six seconds before defenceman Dylan Samberg scored in overtime to complete a thrilling 5-4 comeback victory over the Montreal Canadiens at the Bell Centre. They were coming off arguably the worst defeat in Jets' 2.0 history, falling 7-0 to the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes. Winnipeg looked listless, appearing to quit on itself in what was a ninth consecutive loss. A loss to the Canadiens would have been a 10th straight defeat, giving the Jets two separate double-digit losing skids in the same calendar year after Winnipeg lost 11 consecutive games during the 2025-26 campaign. Instead, the Jets found some last-minute Montreal magic to break the slide, erupting from the bench in pure joy and a large dose of relief. "That felt like a playoff win in there," Jets head coach Scott Arniel said after the game. "I'm so happy for them, and they're so happy for each other. We've been talking about it for the last stretch here, about staying together as a group. We lose together, we win together, but we just stay together. During the first period of Washington’s eventual 6-5 loss, Chychrun went awkwardly into the boards behind the Capitals’ net while making a puck recovery on a power play. The feet-first collision knocked the skate blade out of his right skate and left him immobile right in front of goaltender Logan Thompson . The high-scoring defenseman immediately shouted for help from his teammates and he got it from captain Alex Ovechkin , who propelled Chychrun toward Washington’s bench with a couple of spears to the fallen defender’s rear end. No, that isn’t running back Saquon Barkley executing the Philadelphia Eagles’ famous Tush Push by shoving quarterback Jalen Hurts over the pile to earn a first down; it’s the greatest goal scorer in the history of the NHL jabbing his good pal in the rump to help save the remaining time on Washington’s power play. With Ovechkin’s assistance, the near-helpless Chychrun could quickly get off the ice for repairs, replaced by Cole Hutson with nearly 90 seconds remaining on the man advantage. Ovechkin has recorded plenty of assists during his career, still just two shy of overtaking Nicklas Backstrom for Washington’s all-time franchise lead, but he won’t see his name on the scoresheet for this one. Despite the quicker-than-usual end to his power-play shift and time on the bench to get a new blade installed, Chychrun still led all skaters in the game with 26:50 of ice time. items.body: The Montreal Canadiens were still digesting their epic, history-making collapse a little more than 12 hours later. In a stunning turnaround that made headlines across North America — Fox News called it a "choke job almost too shocking to believe" — the Canadiens surrendered a four-goal lead with 2:39 remaining in regulation and lost 5-4 in overtime to the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday night. "I don't know, it's hard right now," veteran centre Jake Evans said after practice Wednesday morning. "I think we're all still swallowing it up." It was the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history, smashing the previous mark by more than four minutes. Teams had a record of 0-10,299-0 when facing a deficit of at least four goals entering the final three minutes of regulation before Tuesday. The Jets scored four goals in 126 seconds to erase the lead. You have to go back to Jan. 21, 1919, when Montreal gave up four goals in 100 seconds against the Toronto Arenas, to find a faster stretch of four goals against in Canadiens history. "It's hard to explain," said head coach Martin St. Louis, whose playing career spanned 1,134 NHL games. "I've never been part of something like that." St. Louis is known for his optimistic, inspirational approach to coaching. He was relatively calm in his post-game news conference Tuesday but made clear a day later he wasn’t glossing over the jaw-dropping defeat as the Canadiens (9-3-3) prepare to host the Utah Mammoth on Thursday. items.title: How teams and star players would benefit from shorter-term contracts
items.summary: In the flat cap era, every team was chasing contract efficiencies to ice the best rosters. But Justin Bourne writes now that the cap is rising so much, both teams and players should reconsider how they think about contract term.
items.body: Dylan Larkin asked for a trade in year four of an eight-year deal. Connor Hellebuyck asked for a trade in year three of a seven-year deal. Brady Tkachuk made it to year six of his before he wanted out, which was granted before year seven began. All of these players wielded no-trade clauses that hampered any potential return their teams could get, which was a bad deal for the fans twice — they lost a star, and recouped little for him. For these and other elite NHLers, I understand the desire to sign for eight years the second you have a team willing to give it to you. But when it came to these truly top-end guys, the “give me the max dollars and length” always felt like contracts written with crayons rather than calligraphy. Sure you're able to get a big long-term deal, but if you're a proven top-end player in the NHL, wouldn't you want to maintain some flexibility on where you play? The way Auston Matthews has done his contracts has always made sense to me. He's signed five- and four-year contracts after his entry-level deal with the Leafs and has made good money, but never sought out maximum length. Five years is a big commitment to a city, isn’t it? And really, who among us knows what our priorities will be in five years? “I’m happy to re-up when we get there, let’s just re-assess if everyone’s happy” is a thought process I’ve never wavered in defending. items.body: PLANO, Texas — Voters in a Dallas suburb have rejected a proposition that would have authorized new taxes related to a planned new arena for the NHL's Stars. Unofficial results from Tuesday's vote in the city of Plano showed 54.6 per cent of the more than 102,000 votes cast were against the single ballot proposal to authorize taxes on tickets, parking, car rentals, hotel rooms and the professional teams that would use the arena. Those taxes were to help the city pay off up to $700 million in bonds it has committed to the proposed $3 billion mixed-use development that would include the new arena. The vote was about the proposed taxes, and not whether the $1-billion arena could be built as part of a large-scale redevelopment project of The Shops at Willow Bend, where the last enclosed mall built in Texas is being demolished. It could include sports, entertainment, retail, dining and public gathering spaces. “The proposed redevelopment at The Shops at Willow Bend remains an important opportunity for our community," Plano Mayor John Muns said in a statement. “We are committed to thoughtful reinvestment and responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars as we consider what comes next.” The hockey-specific arena would be owned by the city, with the Stars intending to lease it for 30 years. Stars officials hope to move in 2031 about 20 miles north of the downtown American Airlines Center, which they have shared with the NBA’s Dallas Mavericks since it opened in 2001. The leases at the AAC for both teams expire in 2031, and the Mavericks have plans for a similar project of their own away from downtown, about 10 miles north on the former site of a Dallas mall.

items.body: NEWARK, N.J. -- Ryan Nugent-Hopkins felt the significance of his next game and the milestone it represents for the Edmonton Oilers when he saw his teammates Tuesday morning. There they were, all wearing T-shirts that depicted the Oilers forward with a mullet, smoking a cigarette, wearing a short-sleeved camo shirt, and with a tattoo on his arm. On the shirt were the words “1038 games Most Games Played as an Edmonton Oiler.” Nugent-Hopkins hit that mark in a 4-3 shootout loss to the New Jersey Devils at Prudential Center on Tuesday. The 32-year-old forward, selected by Edmonton with the No. 1 pick in the 2011 NHL Draft, passed Kevin Lowe, who played 1,037 games during his 15 seasons with the Oilers. They are the two to have played at least 1,000 games for Edmonton. "I'm very lucky and fortunate to have been able to hit this milestone with this team," Nugent-Hopkins said Tuesday. "It really is a testament to a lot of these guys in this room, and not just the players but the staff, the trainers that have been here for my entire career." After showing him the T-shirts, the Oilers played him a video celebrating his career. "I feel the love," Nugent-Hopkins said. "Having a video that they shared with me was definitely special. To have experienced a lot of these games with a few of the guys in here, it's pretty special. I'm very lucky and fortunate to have been able to hit this milestone with this team." items.title: Jets historic comeback could be the catalyst to save their season
items.summary: The Jets scored five unanswered goals in the final minutes of regulation and OT to beat the Canadiens 5-4.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Winnipeg Jets pulled off one of the greatest regular-season comebacks in NHL history against the Montreal Canadiens Tuesday night, scoring four goals in a two-minute span at the end of the third period to send the game to overtime, where Dylan Samberg sealed it with the OT-winner. The comeback started midway through the third period when Tyrel Bauer took Arber Xhekaj in a fight, followed by captain Adam Lowry dropping the gloves with Florian Xhekaj. The Jets then scored five straight goals on goaltender Jacob Fowler, including two in the final minute by forward Kyle Connor, to complete one of the most shocking results in modern hockey history. On Wednesday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and former NHL goaltender Carter Hutton discuss Winnipeg’s historic win over the Habs and if it saved their season. Tyler Yaremchuk : I don’t know if it’s just in the moment, but this does something. In that room, this is better than if they just won the game 2-1 and squeaked one out that they didn’t deserve. This has to be galvanizing for that group. Carter Hutton : It’s gotta be. The storyline around Tyrel Bauer and Adam Lowry getting in scraps. You’ve got a younger guy in Bauer taking a fight against Arber Xhekaj. Xhekaj knows he’s a younger guy trying to cut his teeth. All of a sudden, Bauer scores a goal to create momentum. They played great and found a way to come back. I think this is a huge moment for the Winnipeg Jets. At a pivotal point where they just lost nine straight, are they going to stick around after they traded Connor Hellebuyck? Or are they going to weed yourself off into the sunset? items.body: André Tourigny got off the plane with scant knowledge of his new home. It was April 2024, and the Arizona Coyotes were abruptly relocating to Utah. items.title: Hellebuyck cites ‘challenging family circumstances’ in letter to Jets fans explaining departure
items.summary: The new Devil netminder had a very unpopular exit from Winnipeg after requesting a trade.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Following a tumultuous exit from Manitoba, former Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck is explaining why he wanted out of town. On his personal Instagram, Hellebuyck wrote a letter to Jets fans, giving the reasons why he requested a trade from the only franchise he’d ever known. Hellebuyck stated that asking to be dealt by the Jets wasn’t an easy decision, but he had his reasons. “I know my decision to request a trade was disappointing and frustrating for many people, especially those who supported me throughout my career,” Hellebuyck wrote. “I understand those feelings, and I want everyone to know it was an extremely difficult decision. There were several considerations that went into my decision, including some very challenging circumstances involving my family. After a lot of thought and discussion, we ultimately felt that making a change was the best thing for our family. We’ve chosen to keep those personal circumstances private, and I hope people can respect that.” The 33-year-old’s wishes were finally granted last month, as the Jets sent Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for forwards Nick Bjugstad, Dawson Mercer and Alexander Command, goaltender Nico Daws, a second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft, and a seventh-rounder in 2027. Hellebuyck did add that Winnipeg will always hold a special place in his heart. “I’ll always be grateful for the life my family and I built there and for the people who became such an important part of it. It’s where I grew as a player and where we started our family. … To the great Jets fans who supported me and my family, thank you. I’ll never forget the pride I felt representing Winnipeg, and I wish the Jets and the entire community nothing but the best.”

The Jets received prospect Alexander Command, forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad, goalie Nico Daws and two draft picks in return. items.summary: Korpisalo has been on injured reserve since the start of the season due to a lower-body injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images A veteran netminder is set to get his wheels under him once again. On Wednesday, the New York Rangers announced that goaltender Joonas Korpisalo has been assigned to their American Hockey League affiliate, the Hartford Wolf Pack, on a conditioning assignment. Per NHL rules, a conditioning stint can last no longer than 14 days. The reason Korpisalo is heading back to the minors is to get in shape after missing a considerable amount of time. The 32-year-old suffered a lower-body injury in the opening days of the 2026-27 season, leading to him being placed on injured reserve. It still isn’t clear when or where Korpisalo suffered the injury. He backed up Igor Shesterkin for the team’s season opener last month. He did appear in one preseason game for the Blueshirts, making 20 saves in a shootout win over the New Jersey Devils. Korpisalo came to Broadway over the summer, as the Boston Bruins traded the Finnish backstop to the Blueshirts for prospect Kalle Vaisanen and a fourth-round pick in the 2028 NHL Draft. Korpisalo had spent the past two seasons with the Bruins, mainly serving as a backup to Jeremy Swayman. In 2025-26, he posted a record of 14-9-6, with a 3.15 goals-against average, a .894 save percentage and one shutout. In 334 regular-season appearances in his NHL career, Korpisalo is 140-126-38, with a 3.06 GAA, a .900 SV% and eight shutouts. He’s in the fourth season of a five-year contract, which he signed with the Ottawa Senators in July 2023. The Wolf Pack are on the road on Wednesday night, facing off against the Washington Capitals ‘ top farm team, the Hershey Bears. Hartford is in the midst of a five-game road trip, which wraps up next Tuesday against the Springfield Falcons.

Because Korpisalo is on the injured reserve, not the long-term injured reserve, the conditioning loan’s duration is governed by Section 13.8 of the NHL’s Collective Bargaining Agreement, not Section 13.9. Section 13.8 stipulates that a standard conditioning loan may last up to 14 consecutive days while keeping the player on the active NHL roster and payroll. In contrast, Section 13.9 states that the LTIR conditioning loan may last up to six days or three games, whichever comes first (teams may request two additional games). In their last official update on Korpisalo’s recovery, the Rangers announced on October 10th that the 12-year netminder was expected to miss another four weeks. items.title: 2027 World Junior Championship: Projecting Canada’s roster
items.summary: After years of missing out on the ultimate prize, will things finally change in Edmonton?
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis Canada hasn’t won World Junior gold since 2023. Given the team’s standards, that’s basically an eternity. It’s been a weird few years for a program that expects excellence. From leaving skilled players at home in favor of grinders to failing to make on-the-fly coaching adjustments, Canada hasn’t gotten it done when it matters most. Will that change in Edmonton this year? On paper, this is the deepest team in the tournament and one that’ll benefit from Sweden being unlikely to get Ivar Stenberg or Anton Frondell. In fact, of the four U-20 players currently in the NHL this year – Matthew Schaefer, Gavin McKenna, Michael Misa and Ben Kindel – none was expected to be available anyway. Last year, there was always a little bit of hope that Kindel, Sam Dickinson and Berkly Catton would be made available. So it’s actually a good situation for the Canadians this year, assuming the multiple AHLers (Brady Martin, Caleb Desnoyers, Braeden Cootes and Jake O’Brien) are loaned out. items.title: IIHF maintains opposition to Russia’s reinstatement, silent on Canada’s position
items.body: The International Ice Hockey Federation says it remains opposed to a ruling ordering Russia's reinstatement to international hockey competition, but has stopped short of addressing Canada's refusal to allow Russian players into the country. Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday that Russian players won't be permitted to compete at next month's world junior championship in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled last week Russia must be reinstated to international competition, starting with the world juniors. Russian teams have been banned since Moscow's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. In a statement Wednesday after a council meeting, the IIHF cited significant logistical, security and competitive challenges with Russia's immediate return, including visa requirements and potential changes to tournament formats. "The global impact of the decision made by the CAS Panel and the challenges it creates for all involved were significantly underestimated," the federation said. The IIHF did not directly address Carney's announcement but said it is consulting national hockey associations, tournament organizers and host authorities before determining its next steps. The federation said its priorities remain the safety of players, officials and fans, along with the smooth operation and integrity of its tournaments. It promised more information in the coming days. Carney said Tuesday that Russian and Belarusian athletes will not be allowed to represent their countries in Canada as long as the war in Ukraine continues. Four years ago, my Hall of Fame player ranking tool, the Pidutti Point Share (PPS) system, got its big break on Daily Faceoff . In the years since, early November has become the ideal time to revisit the Hall trajectories of the NHL’s active stars. Which icons have already secured plaques? It uses era-neutral inputs to equitably measure a player’s career in a single digit, eliminating reputational biases. How does it work? items.summary: It was another game in which the rebuilding Canucks, even with their many flaws, were fully engaged, combative and played their opponents even at five-on-five.
items.body: VANCOUVER — Asked about the opportunity he is getting with the Vancouver Canucks , Jacob Quillan said: “This is everything.” A scoring star in college, the 24-year-old showed Tuesday night he is willing to do anything to stay in the National Hockey League by delivering the hit of the game and then fighting twice as the Canucks lost 5-4 to the Anaheim Ducks at Rogers Arena. Quillan did fine in his first two NHL fights when challenged by six-foot-five Roger McQueen, then rugged defenceman Travis Mitchell. He can’t build his career on fighting. But his willingness to stand up for himself — to show his new Canuck teammates he will fight for them — was notable on a night when Vancouver couldn’t survive its penalty killing or Ducks sniper Cutter Gauthier, but literally and figuratively battled their way back into the game against one of the league’s biggest teams. It was another game in which the rebuilding Canucks, even with their many flaws, were fully engaged, combative and played their opponents even at five-on-five. Down three goals in the third period, the Canucks surged back with a pair of goals from Jake DeBrusk and generated significant offensive-zone pressure at the end. Jonathan Lekkerimaki just missed on a couple of shot-pass redirects from the high slot as Vancouver attacked six-against-five before losing for the 13 th time in 14 games. Their only win during this spiral came a week ago when the Canucks stunned the Ducks in Anaheim by rallying from a three-goal deficit to win 6-5 in overtime, which probably partly explains the feistiness of the rematch. items.title: Canadiens on wrong side of history in skid-stopping comeback win for Jets
items.summary: No matter how poorly the Canadiens played, they were in the best position possible with the clock ticking down, and then they inexcusably crumbled.
items.body: MONTREAL — This was a bad game from start to finish for the Montreal Canadiens , but to suggest it ended the way it should’ve — with the Winnipeg Jets making NHL history to avoid a 10th straight loss — would be bending the truth. For the Canadiens had a 4-0 lead with 2:40 to play, and when Cole Caufield , who scored two of their goals, said it should’ve ended well before they lost in overtime, he was right. No matter how poorly his team played, it was in the best position it could possibly be in with the clock ticking down, and then it inexcusably crumbled. Four Jets goals in 2:39, and one more from Dylan Samberg with 1:30 to go in overtime, sealed the Canadiens’ fate. Afterwards, Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis said, “We got smacked in the teeth and maybe that’s what we needed as a team,” and he was also probably right. If you look at all five games the Canadiens won in succession without Nick Suzuki before this one, a couple of them — including the one at the Heritage Classic in Winnipeg — were hand-delivered by Jacob Fowler . items.body: TORONTO — It seemed like a night in need of a marathon effort. For two periods of this Tuesday night tilt under the Scotiabank Arena lights, the Toronto Maple Leafs looked out of step, out of sorts. items.title: Jets pull record latest four-goal comeback in NHL history to end drought
items.summary: The Jets had lost nine straight games prior to the shocking late-game effort.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources If any Winnipeg Jets fans left the Bell Centre early to beat the traffic, you’re in for a rude awakening. The Jets failed to score through 57:21 against the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday. But after Tyrel Bauer scored his first career goal, everything changed. The Jets ended up scoring three more goals to complete the latest four-goal comeback victory in NHL history. The previous record was set on Nov. 10, 2007, when the Los Angeles Kings scored four goals against Dallas after the 52:46 mark. According to the NHL, this is just the fourth time this has occured after the 50:00 mark, and just the first to have it happen in the final five minutes of a game. Montreal looked in full control, with Owen Beck, Josh Anderson, Cole Caufield (twice) finding the back of the net. Bauer’s goal put an end to Jacob Fowler’s shutout effort, and, seemingly, that felt like the only thing the Jets could get excited about. Instead, Morgan Barron scored less than a minute later, and Kyle Connor made it a one-goal game at 19:00. Just 27 seconds later, Connor recorded his second of the night and 13th of the season, sending the game in overtime after the Jets scored four goals in 2:39 of regulation. Winnipeg wouldn’t stop there. At 3:30 in overtime, Dylan Samberg’s snap shot would beat Fowler to give the Jets the stunning overtime victory, ending the team’s nine-game losing streak in the process. Their last win came on October 13, a 5-2 victory over Minnesota. The Jets finished the game with a 47-22 shot advantage. Notably, this was Montreal’s first game with the club’s new Hometown Remix jersey. The Jets will look to keep the momentum alive on Nov. 5 when the team hosts the Vancouver Canucks.

items.title: NHL Highlights: Stars 6, Capitals 5
items.summary: Jason Robertson had three goals and four points on the night, Roope Hintz added three points and a goal of his own, and the Dallas Stars edged the Washington Capitals 6-5.

items.title: Jack Hughes scores 2 goals as Devils beat Oilers in Connor Hellebuyck's first home start
items.summary: — Jack Hughes scored two goals and had an assist, Connor Hellebuyck made 19 saves to win his first home start of the season and the New Jersey Devils ended the Edmonton Oilers' winning streak at three by winning 4-3 in a shootout on Tuesday night.
